notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR12: "There must not be any entry that contains an OCCURS clause between the descriptions of the data items identified by the data-names in the KEY IS phrase and the subject of the entry." Implemented at 85 for one kind of entry in between: OccursKeyResolvePass.Run resolves each KEY data-name within the table and OccursKeyItemFault walks from the key's parent up to the table entry, reporting COBOL2787 when a group on that path has an OCCURS clause. That walk is the 2023 rule (§2023:13.18.38.3 SR4, a group the key is subordinate to) and has no edition arm. Not implemented for 85: an entry with an OCCURS clause that stands between the subject entry and the key's entry without containing the key (an earlier sibling table, elementary or group, or a table written between two keys). The 1985 sentence bars "any entry", and the narrowing to the key's own hierarchy is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 item 84: "An entry between a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause and the entry describing a data item referenced in the KEY phrase of the OCCURS may itself contain an OCCURS clause, as long as it is not a group item in the hierarchy of the data item referenced in the KEY phrase." Probed at --std 85: refused are a key under 10 G OCCURS 2 (COBOL2787) and a key whose own entry has OCCURS (the neighbouring rule, §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR11); accepted and legal are a table written after the last key, the subject as its own key, and a keyed table inside an outer table; accepted and not legal are 10 S PIC X OCCURS 2 before 10 K, a group 10 GS OCCURS 2 before 10 K3, and 10 S4 PIC X OCCURS 2 between the keys K4A and K4B. The witness puts the key K under 10 G OCCURS 2 TIMES and is refused with COBOL2787.

next.reason: 1985: "There must not be any entry that contains an OCCURS clause between the descriptions of the data items identified by the data-names"; 2023: "If data-name-2 is subordinate to an alphanumeric group item... that group item shall not contain an OCCURS clause.". 1985 bars any OCCURS entry placed between the subject and a KEY item, e.g. an earlier sibling table. 2023 bars OCCURS only in groups that contain data-name-2, so such a sibling is now allowed.
